## What is forecast

Both forecasters forecast a population's *complete* mortality schedule:
single-year logit(q_x) for ages 0–109, female and male, every year ahead.
Both work in the same space, the first principal components of the
effective cores (Step 1 below), and both start from the population's last
observed schedule.  They differ in how they move through that space: MDMx
extrapolates each population's own recent trend, damped and pulled towards
the HMD-wide drift; the flow field moves every population along the paths
that populations at the same level of mortality followed in the past.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What "e₀" means in this chapter and the next
Wherever an unqualified e₀ is quoted (an error, a bias, a coverage), it is
the **average of the female and the male e₀**, $\tfrac12(e_0^F + e_0^M)$, not
the e₀ of a combined-sex life table.
:::

## The MDMx forecaster, step by step

### Step 1 — the space, re-estimated at every origin

Every observed schedule is represented by its effective core
$\G_{c,t} = \bS^\top \M_{c,t}\, \bA$ (chapter 04), an $r_1 \times r_2$
matrix with `{python} r1` × `{python} r2` = `{python} r1 * r2` entries.
Forecasting `{python} r1 * r2` numbers jointly is wasteful, because they
move together: a principal-component analysis (PCA) of the vectorised
cores of all observed country-years (paper §9.1, Eq. 24),

$$
\mathbf{s}_{c,t} = \mathbf{V}^\top\big(\operatorname{vec}(\G_{c,t}) - \bar{\mathbf{g}}\big)
\in \R^{N_{PC}},
$$

with $N_{PC}$ = `{python} SET.n_pc` components, reduces each core to a
handful of *scores*, and the map back to a
schedule is linear (paper Eq. 25):
$\mathbf{z} = \mathbf{z}_{\text{mean}} + \mathbf{L}\,\mathbf{s}$, where
column $j$ of $\mathbf{L}$ is the female and male $\logit(q_x)$ schedule
$\bS\,\mathbf{V}_j\,\bA^\top$ of the $j$-th loading.

A forecast made at origin $o$ must not use any data after $o$.  The bases
$\bS$ and $\bA$, the smoothing of $\bA$, the effective cores and the PCA
are therefore all **re-estimated at each origin from the observed
country-years up to that origin** (`mdmx.forecast.origin_space`), exactly
as chapter 04 estimates them from all the data.  The age rank is held at
the full-data value, $r_2$ = `{python} r2`, at every origin, so that the
forecasts from different origins have the same structure.  For the
latest year in the tensor this reproduces the decomposition of chapter 04
exactly, which the next cell checks.

```{python}
#| label: c11-spaces
#| code-summary: "Re-estimate the bases and the PCA at every origin (cached)"
SPACE_ORIGINS = ORIGINS + [int(years[-1])]
N_PC_MAX = max(F["sens_n_pc"])


def _spaces():
    out = {}
    for o in SPACE_ORIGINS:
        sp = fc.origin_space(M, observed, years, o, tau=SET.tau, age_rank=r2, smooth=SET.smooth,
                             n_pc=N_PC_MAX)
        out[str(o)] = {"U_sex": sp["U_sex"], "U_age": sp["U_age"], "var_share": sp["var_share"],
                       "n_used": int(sp["keep"].sum())}
    return out


spaces = artifacts.stage(
    "forecast_spaces", _spaces, inputs=["tensor"],
    params={**SET.as_dict(), "origins": SPACE_ORIGINS, "n_pc": N_PC_MAX},
    code=[_spaces, *fc.SPACE_CODE],
    desc="Sex/age bases and PCA of the effective cores re-estimated at each forecast origin")

full = spaces[str(years[-1])]
check = max(np.abs(full["U_age"] - tucker["U_age"]).max(), np.abs(full["U_sex"] - tucker["U_sex"]).max())
print(f"Bases from all data vs the decomposition artefact: max |difference| = {check:.1e}")
assert check < 1e-10, "the full-data space must reproduce chapter 04"

n = SET.n_pc
pca_tab = pd.DataFrame([{"origin": int(o), "country-years": sp["n_used"],
                         "PC1 (%)": 100 * sp["var_share"][0],
                         f"PC1–{n} (%)": 100 * sp["var_share"][:n].sum(),
                         f"PC1–{N_PC_MAX} (%)": 100 * sp["var_share"][:N_PC_MAX].sum()}
                        for o, sp in spaces.items()])
print(pca_tab.round(2).to_string(index=False))

cv_shares = pca_tab[pca_tab["origin"].isin(ORIGINS)][f"PC1–{n} (%)"]
latex.report("fcCoreDim", r1 * r2, desc="Elements of an effective core (r1 x r2)")
latex.report("fcCoreStateDim", 2 * r1 * r2, desc="State dimension of a Kalman filter on the full core")
latex.report("fcNPc", n, desc="PCA scores forecast (N_PC)")
latex.report("fcStateDim", 2 * n, desc="State dimension of the MDMx Kalman filter")
latex.report("fcNParams", 3 * n + 1, desc="Kalman hyperparameters per population (3 N_PC + 1)")
latex.report("fcPcaVarFirst", 100 * full["var_share"][0], digits=1,
             desc="Percent of core variance on PC1 (all observed country-years)")
latex.report("fcPcaVarCum", 100 * full["var_share"][:n].sum(), digits=1,
             desc="Percent of core variance on the first N_PC PCs (all observed country-years)")
latex.report("fcPcaVarCumMin", cv_shares.min(), digits=1, desc="Min over CV origins of that percent")
latex.report("fcPcaVarCumMax", cv_shares.max(), digits=1, desc="Max over CV origins of that percent")
```

The first component carries most of the variation — it is essentially the
overall level of mortality — and the first `{python} n` together carry
`{python} num("fcPcaVarCum")`% of the variance of the cores of all observed
country-years (`{python} num("fcPcaVarCumMin")`–`{python} num("fcPcaVarCumMax")`%
in the space estimated on the data up to each of the origins illustrated here,
every `{python} ORIGINS[1] - ORIGINS[0]` years from `{python} ORIGINS[0]` to
`{python} ORIGINS[-1]`).  The remainder is not lost for the history — it is in
the observed data — but a forecast can only move in the space of the
first `{python} n` components.  We return to what that costs at the
forecast's jump-off below.

### Step 2 — the drift target

Each population's own recent trend is informative, but noisy; the average
trend of all HMD populations is stable, but ignores what is particular to
the population.  MDMx blends the two (paper §9.2.1):

$$
\boldsymbol\delta_{\text{hier}} = w_{\text{HMD}}\,\boldsymbol\delta_{\text{HMD}}
 + w_{\text{country}}\,\boldsymbol\delta_{c},
$$

with weights $w_{\text{HMD}}$ = `{python} SET.weight_hmd` and
$w_{\text{country}}$ = `{python} SET.weight_country`.
A population's drift $\boldsymbol\delta_c$ is the average change of its
scores per **calendar year** over the window $[o-W, o]$, with
$W$ = `{python} SET.drift_window` years, measured between its first and last
observed years in the window (`mdmx.forecast.country_drifts`); missing and
exceptional years inside the window are simply not used, and the elapsed
time is counted in calendar years.  A population needs at least
`{python} SET.drift_min_years` observed years in the window for its drift
to count.  $\boldsymbol\delta_{\text{HMD}}$ is the average of the drifts of
all populations with a defined drift at that origin.  The target has no regime
level (paper §9.2.1), so this chapter does not depend on the clustering of
chapter 06.

### Step 3 — the drift-constrained Kalman filter

For each PCA score the model is a damped local linear trend whose drift
reverts not to zero but to the target (paper §9.2.2, Eqs. 26–27):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell_t &= \ell_{t-1} + \delta_{t-1} + \eta^{\ell}_t, &\operatorname{var}\eta^\ell &= q^\ell,\\
\delta_t &= \rho\,\delta_{t-1} + (1-\rho)\,\delta_{\text{hier}} + \eta^{\delta}_t,
  &\operatorname{var}\eta^\delta &= q^\delta,\\
y_t &= \ell_t + \varepsilon_t, &\operatorname{var}\varepsilon &= r,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $y_t$ is the observed score in calendar year $t$.  With $\rho<1$ the
forecast drift converges geometrically to the target, so a long-range
forecast follows the blended trend whatever the population did in its
last few years.  The covariances are diagonal, so the
`{python} n` components are independent two-state filters that share
$\rho$; `mdmx.forecast.llt_filter` writes this out and is checked against
the textbook matrix filter in `tests/test_forecast.py`.

The filter runs over **every calendar year** from the population's first
observed year to the origin.  In a year without an observed schedule —
a war or epidemic year set aside as exceptional, or a year missing from
the HMD series — the update step is skipped: the state is carried forward by
the model and its uncertainty grows, exactly as in a forecast.  The
$3N_{PC}+1$ = `{python} 3 * n + 1` parameters ($q^\ell$, $q^\delta$, $r$ for
each component, and the common $\rho$, kept between
`{python} SET.rho_bounds[0]` and `{python} SET.rho_bounds[1]`) maximise the Gaussian likelihood of the
observed years (prediction-error decomposition) by L-BFGS-B.  Many of
these maxima lie on a bound — a variance at its floor, which is effectively
zero, or $\rho$ at its lower bound — so the optimiser works on the standard
deviations and on $\rho$ itself, where such a maximum can be reached.  It
runs until $-\log L$ stops decreasing at machine precision, and a fit
counts as converged if the projected gradient there is below
`{python} f"{SET.mle_pg_flag:g}"`.
The likelihood can have more than one local maximum — typically one with
$\rho$ at its lower bound and a higher one inside the range — so the
optimiser is started from several points and the best fit is kept:
moment-based starting values ($q^\ell = \operatorname{var}\Delta y$,
$q^\delta = \operatorname{var}\Delta^2 y/4$, $r = \operatorname{var}\Delta y/10$,
within their bounds) with $\rho$ in the middle of its range and at
`{python} len(SET.mle_rho_starts)` fixed levels across
it, and the `{python} SET.mle_grid_top` best points of the *profile*
likelihood of $\rho$ on a grid of `{python} len(SET.mle_grid_rho)` values.
Given $\rho$, the components are independent, so the profile is cheap: the
standard deviations are found component by component by a grid search and
then fitted exactly at every grid value of $\rho$ at once.  Several starts
make a missed maximum unlikely, not impossible; the design was chosen by comparing
search strategies.  Chapter 12 reports convergence and the fitted $\rho$ by
origin for every fit of the evaluation, under both fitting periods.  How
often a single start would have missed the maximum is counted
[below](#sec-c11-starts) for the fits of the long-run forecasts, one per
population at the latest data year.

The cell below shows one fit: France at the 1960 origin, whose training
series has gaps at both world wars.

```{python}
#| label: fig-c11-filter-example
#| fig-cap: "The filter on a series with gaps: the first two PCA scores of France (total population) up to 1960 (points; shaded years have no observed schedule — war years are exceptional) and the forecast from 1960 (line: mean; band: 95% prediction interval of the observed score, before any calibration)."
EX_POP, EX_ORIGIN = "FRATNP", 1960
ex_space = fc.origin_space(M, observed, years, EX_ORIGIN, tau=SET.tau, age_rank=r2,
                           smooth=SET.smooth, n_pc=n)
ex_drifts = fc.country_drifts(ex_space["scores"], years, EX_ORIGIN, SET.drift_window,
                              SET.drift_min_years)
c = PIDX[EX_POP]
t_first = int(np.flatnonzero(ex_space["keep"][c])[0])
t_o = int(np.flatnonzero(years == EX_ORIGIN)[0])
y_ex = ex_space["scores"][c, t_first:t_o + 1]
target, _ = fc.drift_target(ex_drifts, c, SET.weight_hmd, SET.weight_country)
ex_fit = fc.fit_llt(y_ex, target, np.maximum(np.nanvar(ex_drifts, axis=0), 1e-8), SET)
mean, var = fc.llt_forecast(ex_fit["state"], ex_fit["rho"], ex_fit["q_level"], ex_fit["q_drift"],
                            ex_fit["r"], target, SET.horizon)
yrs_ex = years[t_first:t_o + 1]
fc_yrs = EX_ORIGIN + np.arange(1, SET.horizon + 1)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8))
for j, ax in enumerate(axes):
    for yr in yrs_ex[~np.isfinite(y_ex[:, 0])]:
        ax.axvspan(yr - 0.5, yr + 0.5, color=plotting.COLORS["grey"], alpha=0.25, lw=0)
    ax.plot(yrs_ex, y_ex[:, j], ".", ms=3, color=plotting.COLORS["observed"])
    ax.plot(fc_yrs, mean[:, j], color=COLOR["MDMx"])
    half = Z[95] * np.sqrt(var[:, j])
    ax.fill_between(fc_yrs, mean[:, j] - half, mean[:, j] + half, color=COLOR["MDMx"], alpha=0.25)
    ax.set_title(f"PC{j + 1} score", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
plt.show()
print(f"{NAME[EX_POP]}, origin {EX_ORIGIN}: {np.isfinite(y_ex[:, 0]).sum()} observed of "
      f"{len(y_ex)} calendar years; ρ = {ex_fit['rho']:.3f}; "
      f"{ex_fit['n_iter']} iterations, converged: {ex_fit['converged']}")
```

### Step 4 — from scores to schedules and e₀

A forecast of the scores is a forecast of the complete female and male
schedules, $\hat{\mathbf z}_{o+h} = \mathbf z_{\text{mean}} + \mathbf L\,
\hat{\mathbf s}_{o+h}$, and from those of e₀ for each sex.  The forecast
uncertainty of the scores at horizon $h$ is that of a future *observed*
score: the filter's state variance plus the observation noise $r$ (both
diagonal).  Because e₀ is a nonlinear function of the schedule, its
standard deviation follows from the delta method (paper §9.2):
$\sigma^2_{e_0}(h) = \sum_j J_j^2 \operatorname{var}(s_j)$ with
$J = \partial e_0/\partial \mathbf s = (\partial e_0/\partial\mathbf z)\,\mathbf L$.
The gradient $\partial e_0/\partial\mathbf z$ is computed exactly from the
life table (`mdmx.forecast.e0_and_gradient`): with
$e_0 = \sum_k w_k l_k$, $\partial e_0/\partial z_x = -q_x\sum_{k>x} w_k l_k$.
A Monte-Carlo check of the delta method is reported with the intervals.

### Step 5 — the jump-off anchor {#sec-fc-anchor}

The Kalman filter starts the forecast from the *filtered* level of the
scores, and the `{python} SET.n_pc` scores represent a schedule only up to
the PCA truncation.  The schedule the forecast starts from therefore differs
from the observed one, by a small amount at most ages but enough to move the
female − male gap of e₀ at the jump-off.  MDMx keeps the part of the observed schedule that
its scores do not represent (paper §9.2.4, Eq. 28): the residual of the observed schedule at the
job's last training year from its projection on the scores,
$\varepsilon_{c} = \mathrm{logit}\,q_{c,t_0} - (\bar z + L\,s_{c,t_0})$, is
added to every forecast schedule (`forecast.mdmx_origin(anchor="persistent")`,
the persistent anchor, ρ = 1).  The flow field uses
the same anchor.  A decaying anchor, with a half-life of
`{python} f"{float(E['decaying_anchor_half_life']):g}"` years, is a sensitivity in chapter 12.

The residual holds two things: the population's own detail, which the anchor
is there to keep, and the noise of that one year's single-age rates, which it
is not.  Carried as observed, the noise would stay in every forecast schedule
at every horizon.  The residual is therefore smoothed over age before it is
added, each sex's by a Whittaker smoother with second differences,
$\tilde\varepsilon = \arg\min_{u} \sum_x (u_x - \varepsilon_x)^2 + \nu \sum_x (\Delta^2 u_x)^2$
over ages 1 and over, with ν = `{python} f"{SET.anchor_smoothing:,.0f}"`; age 0 keeps
its observed value, because the step from infancy to childhood is real
(`forecast.smooth_residual`).  Both forecasters carry $\tilde\varepsilon_c$.
The smoothing was chosen on the evaluation's origins up to 2000, among
smoothers over age and over years, of the sex difference and of each sex;
chapter 12 shows what it does to the comparison's measures.

At every origin of the evaluation, the cell measures what the anchor keeps:
the e₀ and the gap of the projection plus the smoothed residual minus those of
the projection, and the share of the residual that the smoothing removes.

## The flow field

The flow field (paper §9.3) forecasts in MDMx's space (Step 1), from data up to the
origin only (`mdmx.flowfield`).  Its state is the vector of PCA scores of a
population-year, $s = (s_1, \dots, s_5)$; the first score is the level of
mortality, oriented so that a higher $s_1$ is lower mortality.

1. **The speed** (`flowfield.speed_function`).  Each population's $s_1$ is
   smoothed over its observed years, and its annual change is computed.  The
   speed $g(s_1)$ is a LOWESS of these changes against $s_1$, pooled over the
   populations: how fast populations at each level of mortality improved.
   It is never allowed to reverse the improvement.
2. **The frontier point** (`flowfield.orientation`).  $s_1^*$ is the median
   $s_1$ of the population-years whose e₀ is in the top
   `{python} f"{1 - FFS.frontier_quantile:.0%}"`.  Below it a
   forecast moves at the pace that populations at its level moved in the
   past.  Beyond it there is no past to learn from.
3. **The pace beyond the frontier** (`flowfield.frontier_level`,
   `frontier_speed`, `frontier_rule`).  In each year the `{python} FFS.frontier_k`
   populations with the highest e₀ lead; their mean $s_1$, chain-linked so that
   populations entering the data do not move it, gives the frontier's pace
   $V_s$ over the `{python} FFS.frontier_window` years before the origin.  Beyond
   $s_1^*$ the speed is $v_1 = \max\{0,\, w V_s + (1 - w)\, g(s_1^*)\}$, with
   $w = n/(n + n_0)$, $n_0$ = `{python} f"{FFS.frontier_n0:g}"`, for the $n$
   populations that led in those years.
4. **The shape law** (`flowfield.shape_law`).  The other scores follow
   $s_1$ along $f_k(s_1)$, a LOWESS of $s_k$ on $s_1$ over the last
   `{python} FFS.shape_window` years
   (along its tangent beyond the frontier point of those years), and a
   population's own deviation from $f_k$ decays at the pooled rate $\alpha_k$
   a year.
5. **The path** (`flowfield.integrate`, `forecast_origin`).  From the last
   observed scores, $s_1$ moves one year at a time at the speed of its level,
   the other scores follow the shape law, and the schedules carry the
   jump-off anchor with its smoothed residual (Step 5).

The form (the speed on every year, the shape law on the last 50, the
leaders' pace beyond the frontier) was chosen in development studies on the
development origins; chapter 12 describes how (the article's §10.9 says on which origins the form was selected).  The figure shows the flow fitted to every year up to the latest data.

```{python}
#| label: c11-flow
#| code-summary: "The flow at the latest data year; the flow and the anchor's residual at every origin of the evaluation (cached)"
last = int(years[-1])
E0 = ff.e0_matrix(M, observed)
space_last = fc.origin_space(M, observed, years, last, tau=SET.tau, age_rank=r2, smooth=SET.smooth, n_pc=SET.n_pc)
speed_last = ff.speed_function(space_last["scores"], space_last["keep"], years, E0, FFS)
shape_last = ff.shape_law(space_last["scores"], ff._window(space_last["keep"], years, last, FFS.shape_window),
                          years, E0, FFS)
flow_last = ff.build_flow(space_last["scores"], space_last["keep"], years, E0, last, FFS)
eval_jobs = fc.cv_jobs(observed, pops, years, list(DESIGN.origins), DESIGN.horizon, DESIGN.min_train_years,
                       DESIGN.min_test_years)


def _by_origin():
    rows, resid = [], []
    for o, jo in eval_jobs.groupby("origin"):
        sp = fc.origin_space(M, observed, years, int(o), tau=SET.tau, age_rank=r2, smooth=SET.smooth, n_pc=SET.n_pc)
        rows.append({"origin": int(o), **ff.flow_summary(ff.build_flow(sp["scores"], sp["keep"], years, E0, int(o),
                                                                       FFS))})
        for job in jo.itertuples():
            c, t0 = PIDX[job.pop], int(np.flatnonzero(years == job.last_train_year)[0])
            z_proj = fc.scores_to_logit(sp["scores"][c, t0], sp["z_mean"], sp["L"])
            r_obs = M[:, :, c, t0] - z_proj
            r_kept = fc.smooth_residual(r_obs, SET.anchor_smoothing)
            e_kept, e_proj = lifetable.e0_from_logit(z_proj + r_kept), lifetable.e0_from_logit(z_proj)
            resid.append({"origin": int(o), "pop": job.pop, "de0": float(e_kept.mean() - e_proj.mean()),
                          "dgap": float((e_kept[0] - e_kept[1]) - (e_proj[0] - e_proj[1])),
                          "medabs": float(np.median(np.abs(r_obs))),
                          "removed": float(1 - np.sum(r_kept ** 2) / np.sum(r_obs ** 2))})
    return {"flows": pd.DataFrame(rows), "residuals": pd.DataFrame(resid)}


by_origin = artifacts.stage("forecast_flow_origins", _by_origin, inputs=["tensor"],
                            params={"mdmx": SET.as_dict(), "flowfield": FFS.as_dict(), "design": DESIGN.as_dict()},
                            code=[_by_origin, *ff.FLOW_CODE],
                            desc="The flow field's parameters and the anchor's residual at every origin")
FLOWS, RESID = by_origin["flows"], by_origin["residuals"]
latex.report("fcAnchorGapMedAbs", float(RESID["dgap"].abs().median()), digits=2,
             desc="Median |change of the female-male e0 gap| the anchor keeps at the jump-off (years)")
latex.report("fcAnchorEzeroMedAbs", float(RESID["de0"].abs().median()), digits=3,
             desc="Median |change of e0 (average)| the anchor keeps at the jump-off (years)")
latex.report("fcAnchorLogitMedAbs", float(RESID["medabs"].median()), digits=3,
             desc="Median over jobs of the median |residual| in logit(qx) at the jump-off, as observed")
latex.report("fcAnchorSmoothing", SET.anchor_smoothing, text=f"{SET.anchor_smoothing:,.0f}",
             desc="Penalty nu of the Whittaker smoother of the anchor's jump-off residual")
latex.report("fcAnchorRemovedPct", 100 * float(RESID["removed"].median()), digits=0,
             desc="Median over jobs of the share (%) of the jump-off residual's sum of squares that the smoothing "
                  "removes")
fl = ff.flow_summary(flow_last)
latex.report("fcFlowStarLast", fl["s1_star"], digits=2, desc=f"Frontier point s1* (oriented) at {last}")
latex.report("fcFlowVOneLast", fl["v1"], digits=3, desc=f"Speed beyond s1* (oriented s1 per year) at {last}")
latex.report("fcFlowWLast", fl["w"], digits=2, desc=f"Shrinkage weight w = n/(n + n0) at {last}")
latex.report("fcAnchorHalfLife", E["decaying_anchor_half_life"], text=f"{float(E['decaying_anchor_half_life']):g}",
             desc="Half-life (years) of the decaying anchor of the sensitivity analysis")
# The flow field's settings (config/params.d/flowfield.toml), as the paper quotes them.
latex.report("fcFlowFrontierTopPct", 100 * (1 - FFS.frontier_quantile), digits=0,
             desc="Top percent of country-years by e0 whose median level is the frontier point")
latex.report("fcFlowSmoothYears", FFS.smooth_years, desc="Fewest observed years each local fit of a population's level spans")
latex.report("fcFlowSmoothFracMin", 100 * FFS.smooth_frac_min, digits=0,
             desc="Smallest span (%) of the LOWESS of a population's level, as a share of its observed years")
latex.report("fcFlowSmoothLongYears", int(round(FFS.smooth_years / FFS.smooth_frac_min)),
             desc="Observed years beyond which the smallest span, not the fewest years, sets the LOWESS span")
latex.report("fcFlowMinYears", FFS.min_years,
             desc="Observed years a population needs for the speed, the shape law and the relaxation")
latex.report("fcFlowSpan", FFS.speed_frac, digits=1, desc="LOWESS span of the speed and of the shape law")
latex.report("fcFlowFrontierK", FFS.frontier_k, desc="Leading populations in each year (m)")
latex.report("fcFlowFrontierWindow", FFS.frontier_window, desc="Years up to the origin of the leaders' pace")
latex.report("fcFlowFrontierNzero", FFS.frontier_n0, text=f"{FFS.frontier_n0:g}",
             desc="Shrinkage constant n0 of the leaders' pace")
latex.report("fcFlowFrontierMinYears", FFS.frontier_min_years,
             desc="Years with a frontier level the window needs for rule FR1 (otherwise FR0)")
latex.report("fcFlowShapeWindow", FFS.shape_window, desc="Years up to the origin of the shape law")
latex.report("fcFlowTangentPct", 100 * FFS.tangent_share, digits=0,
             desc="Percent of the range of s1 before the frontier point over which the shape law's tangent is fitted")
latex.report("fcFlowRelaxMaxLag", FFS.relax_max_lag, desc="Largest calendar lag of the relaxation's autocorrelations")
latex.report("fcFlowRelaxMinBeta", FFS.relax_min_beta, digits=2,
             desc="Autocorrelation above which a lag enters the relaxation's fit")
latex.report("fcFlowIntervalMinPoints", FFS.interval_min_points,
             desc="Errors a cell needs for an empirical interval of the flow field")
print(f"At the jump-off the anchor keeps a median |Δ gap| of {RESID['dgap'].abs().median():.2f} y "
      f"and |Δ e0| of {RESID['de0'].abs().median():.3f} y ({len(RESID)} jobs); the smoothing removes a median "
      f"{100 * RESID['removed'].median():.0f} % of the residual's sum of squares")
```

### What the fitted flow says about mortality change

The flow field's fitted objects can be read as statements about how mortality
changes.  Read together, the speed and the shape law trace one path through
the space of schedules, the *typical path*: the level $s_1$ moves at the speed
$g(s_1)$ and the other scores sit on the shape law.  One year along it the
level moves to $s_1 + g(s_1)$, so the gain in e₀ that the flow implies at the
level $s_1$ is $e(s_1 + g(s_1)) - e(s_1)$, where $e(s_1)$ is the e₀ of the
typical schedule at that level (paper §11.4, Eq. 37).  Plotted against e₀,
this implied gain is the flow field's phase portrait of life expectancy: the
counterpart of bayesLife's gain function, estimated over the whole schedule
and without a parametric form.  The typical path also gives each sex's e₀, so
the gap between the sexes along the level of mortality.

The section describes the whole transition, so it uses the flow at the latest
data year with the shape law estimated on every year (`config/params.d/theory.toml`).
The forecaster's shape law uses the last 50 years only, when few populations
were at the lower levels.  Observed gains are centred over 10 years.

```{python}
#| label: c11-theory
#| code-summary: "The typical path of the flow fitted to every year, and the observed gains and gaps"
TH = P.section("theory")
FFS_ALL = ff.FlowFieldSettings.from_params(
    P.section("flowfield"), shape_window=None if TH["shape_window"] == "all" else int(TH["shape_window"]))
flow_all = ff.build_flow(space_last["scores"], space_last["keep"], years, E0, last, FFS_ALL)
s1_raw = space_last["scores"][..., 0][space_last["keep"]]
grid = np.linspace(s1_raw.min(), s1_raw.max(), int(TH["grid_points"]))
PATH = theory.typical_path(flow_all, space_last["z_mean"], space_last["L"], grid)
OBS = theory.observed_levels(M, observed, years, pops, int(TH["gain_half_window"]))
BANDS = theory.binned_medians(OBS, "e0", ["gain", "gap", "year"], TH["bands"])
LEV = theory.at_levels(PATH, TH["levels"], ["gain", "gap"])
by_s1 = PATH.sort_values("s1")
front_e0 = float(np.interp(flow_all["sign"] * flow_all["s1_star"], by_s1["s1"], by_s1["e0"]))
w = int(TH["gain_half_window"])
latex.report("fcTheoryGainYears", 2 * w, desc="Years over which an observed gain in e0 is centred")
latex.report("fcTheoryEzeroMin", PATH["e0"].min(), digits=0, desc="Lowest e0 on the typical path (years)")
latex.report("fcTheoryEzeroMax", PATH["e0"].max(), digits=0, desc="Highest e0 on the typical path (years)")
i_gain, i_gap = PATH["gain"].idxmax(), PATH["gap"].idxmax()
latex.report("fcTheoryGainPeak", PATH.loc[i_gain, "gain"], digits=2,
             desc="Largest implied annual gain in e0 on the typical path (years per year)")
latex.report("fcTheoryGainPeakEzero", PATH.loc[i_gain, "e0"], digits=0, desc="e0 at the largest implied gain (years)")
latex.report("fcTheoryGapPeak", PATH.loc[i_gap, "gap"], digits=1,
             desc="Largest female minus male e0 gap on the typical path (years)")
latex.report("fcTheoryGapPeakEzero", PATH.loc[i_gap, "e0"], digits=0, desc="e0 at the largest gap (years)")
latex.report("fcTheoryFrontierEzero", front_e0, digits=0,
             desc="e0 of the typical schedule at the frontier point of the flow fitted to every year (years)")
for row in LEV.itertuples():
    tag = latex.number_word(int(row.e0))
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryGainAt{tag}", row.gain, digits=2,
                 desc=f"Implied annual gain in e0 on the typical path at e0 = {row.e0:g} (years per year)")
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryGapAt{tag}", row.gap, digits=1,
                 desc=f"Female minus male e0 gap on the typical path at e0 = {row.e0:g} (years)")
for row in BANDS.itertuples():
    tag = latex.number_word(int(row.low)) + latex.number_word(int(row.high))
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsGain{tag}", row.gain, digits=2,
                 desc=f"Median observed centred gain in e0, e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}] (years per year)")
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsGap{tag}", row.gap, digits=1,
                 desc=f"Median observed female minus male e0 gap, e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}] (years)")
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsYear{tag}", row.year, text=latex.fmt_year(latex.round_half_up(row.year)),
                 desc=f"Median calendar year of the observed country-years with e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}]")
latex.report("fcTheoryObsGainN", int(OBS["gain"].notna().sum()), desc="Country-years with an observed centred gain")
latex.report("fcTheoryObsN", len(OBS), desc="Observed country-years in the theory figure")
# How many populations the forecaster's shape law sees at the lower levels, in its own window.
in_window = OBS[OBS["year"] > last - FFS.shape_window]
low = float(TH["low_level"])
latex.report("fcTheoryLowLevel", low, digits=0, desc="e0 below which the forecaster's shape law has few populations")
latex.report("fcTheoryLowPops", int(in_window.loc[in_window["e0"] < low, "pop"].nunique()),
             desc=f"Populations observed below e0 {low:g} in the last {FFS.shape_window} years")
latex.report("fcTheoryWindowPops", int(in_window["pop"].nunique()),
             desc=f"Populations observed in the last {FFS.shape_window} years")
# The dip of the implied gain inside a band of e0, and its recovery up to the frontier point.
def dip(path, band, front):
    """The smallest implied gain with e0 inside ``band`` and its e0; then the largest gain after it up to the
    frontier point, and its e0 (the recovery)."""
    seg = path[path["e0"].between(*band)]
    i = seg["gain"].idxmin()
    low, low_e0 = float(seg.loc[i, "gain"]), float(seg.loc[i, "e0"])
    after = path[(path["e0"] > low_e0) & (path["e0"] <= front)]
    j = after["gain"].idxmax()
    return low, low_e0, float(after.loc[j, "gain"]), float(after.loc[j, "e0"])


DIP_BAND = [float(x) for x in TH["dip_band"]]


def report_dip(path, front, tag, what):
    low, low_e0, high, high_e0 = dip(path, DIP_BAND, front)
    band = f"e0 {DIP_BAND[0]:.0f}-{DIP_BAND[1]:.0f}"
    latex.report(f"fcTheory{tag}GainDip", low, digits=2, desc=f"{what}: smallest implied gain with {band}")
    latex.report(f"fcTheory{tag}GainDipEzero", low_e0, digits=0, desc=f"{what}: e0 at that smallest gain (years)")
    latex.report(f"fcTheory{tag}GainRecover", high, digits=2,
                 desc=f"{what}: largest implied gain after it, up to the frontier point")
    latex.report(f"fcTheory{tag}GainRecoverEzero", high_e0, digits=0, desc=f"{what}: e0 at that largest gain (years)")


report_dip(PATH, front_e0, "", "Every population")
# Without the populations of Central and Eastern Europe (theory.toml), whose long stagnation and reversal
# of male mortality fall at these levels: the flow refitted without them, and the medians of both groups.
CEE = [p_ for p_ in TH["central_eastern"] if p_ in PIDX]
keep_o = space_last["keep"].copy()
keep_o[[PIDX[p_] for p_ in CEE]] = False
flow_o = ff.build_flow(space_last["scores"], keep_o, years, E0, last, FFS_ALL)
s1_o = space_last["scores"][..., 0][keep_o]
PATH_O = theory.typical_path(flow_o, space_last["z_mean"], space_last["L"],
                             np.linspace(s1_o.min(), s1_o.max(), int(TH["grid_points"])))
by_s1_o = PATH_O.sort_values("s1")
front_o = float(np.interp(flow_o["sign"] * flow_o["s1_star"], by_s1_o["s1"], by_s1_o["e0"]))
LEV_O = theory.at_levels(PATH_O, [x for x in TH["levels"] if PATH_O["e0"].min() <= x <= PATH_O["e0"].max()],
                         ["gain", "gap"])
OBS["cee"] = OBS["pop"].isin(CEE)
BANDS_O = theory.binned_medians(OBS[~OBS["cee"]], "e0", ["gain", "gap", "year"], TH["bands"])
BANDS_C = theory.binned_medians(OBS[OBS["cee"]], "e0", ["gain", "gap", "year"], TH["bands"])
latex.report("fcTheoryCeePops", len(CEE), desc="Populations of Central and Eastern Europe (theory.toml)")
i_go, i_po = PATH_O["gain"].idxmax(), PATH_O["gap"].idxmax()
latex.report("fcTheoryOtherGainPeak", PATH_O.loc[i_go, "gain"], digits=2,
             desc="Without Central and Eastern Europe: largest implied gain on the typical path")
latex.report("fcTheoryOtherGainPeakEzero", PATH_O.loc[i_go, "e0"], digits=0, desc="… and its e0")
latex.report("fcTheoryOtherGapPeak", PATH_O.loc[i_po, "gap"], digits=1,
             desc="Without Central and Eastern Europe: largest sex gap on the typical path (years)")
latex.report("fcTheoryOtherGapPeakEzero", PATH_O.loc[i_po, "e0"], digits=0, desc="… and its e0")
report_dip(PATH_O, front_o, "Other", "Without Central and Eastern Europe")
for row in LEV_O.itertuples():
    tag = latex.number_word(int(row.e0))
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryOtherGainAt{tag}", row.gain, digits=2,
                 desc=f"Without Central and Eastern Europe: implied gain at e0 = {row.e0:g} (years per year)")
    latex.report(f"fcTheoryOtherGapAt{tag}", row.gap, digits=1,
                 desc=f"Without Central and Eastern Europe: sex gap on the typical path at e0 = {row.e0:g} (years)")
for name, tab in (("Other", BANDS_O), ("Cee", BANDS_C)):
    for row in tab.itertuples():
        tag = latex.number_word(int(row.low)) + latex.number_word(int(row.high))
        who = "the other populations" if name == "Other" else "Central and Eastern Europe"
        if np.isfinite(row.gain):
            latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsGain{name}{tag}", row.gain, digits=2,
                         desc=f"Median observed gain in e0, {who}, e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}]")
        latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsGap{name}{tag}", row.gap, digits=1,
                     desc=f"Median observed sex gap, {who}, e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}]")
        latex.report(f"fcTheoryObsYear{name}{tag}", row.year, text=latex.fmt_year(latex.round_half_up(row.year)),
                     desc=f"Median year of the observed country-years, {who}, e0 in ({row.low:g}, {row.high:g}]")
print(LEV.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(BANDS.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("Without Central and Eastern Europe:"); print(LEV_O.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(BANDS_O.round(3).to_string(index=False)); print(BANDS_C.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("Below", low, "in the window:", sorted(in_window.loc[in_window["e0"] < low, "pop"].unique()))
```

The implied gain rises with e₀ to `{python} num("fcTheoryGainPeak")` years a
year at e₀ `{python} num("fcTheoryGainPeakEzero")`, dips to
`{python} num("fcTheoryGainDip")` at e₀ `{python} num("fcTheoryGainDipEzero")`, recovers to
`{python} num("fcTheoryGainRecover")` at `{python} num("fcTheoryGainRecoverEzero")` and declines
to `{python} num("fcTheoryGainAtEighty")` at 80.  The dip is mostly the populations of Central and
Eastern Europe: their median observed gain at e₀ 65–70 is
`{python} num("fcTheoryObsGainCeeSixtyfiveSeventy")` years a year (median year
`{python} num("fcTheoryObsYearCeeSixtyfiveSeventy")`), against
`{python} num("fcTheoryObsGainOtherSixtyfiveSeventy")` for the other populations.  Refitted
without them, the flow's gain is `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGainAtSeventy")` at e₀ 70; its dip
is `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGainDip")` at `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGainDipEzero")` and it
reaches `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGainRecover")` at `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGainRecoverEzero")`.
The gap between the sexes on the typical path is about
`{python} num("fcTheoryGapAtFortyfive")` years at e₀ 45, peaks at
`{python} num("fcTheoryGapPeak")` years at e₀ `{python} num("fcTheoryGapPeakEzero")`
(`{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGapPeak")` at `{python} num("fcTheoryOtherGapPeakEzero")` without
Central and Eastern Europe) and narrows to `{python} num("fcTheoryGapAtEighty")` at 80.  Paper
§11.4 ("What the flow field says about mortality change") interprets these against the
literature.

## Sex differences in the long run

MDMx forecasts both sexes at every age from one set of scores, so the age
pattern of the sex difference is forecast jointly — not held fixed by
assumption, as in the coherent FDM (whose sex ratios are stationary), nor
left free, as in Lee–Carter and Hyndman–Ullah.  How does it behave far
ahead?  The forecast drift of the scores reverts to the hierarchical
target δ_hier (Step 3), so in the long run the male − female difference of
logit(q_x) at age x changes at the constant rate
$(L_{\text{male}} - L_{\text{female}})\,\delta_{\text{hier}}$
(`mdmx.compare.sex_difference_slope`).  On the logit scale any non-zero
rate means that the difference keeps changing, so the question is how
fast.  The cell computes the rate for every population at the latest data
year, `{python} int(years[-1])` — split into the part that comes from the
HMD-wide drift (common to the populations) and the population's own
part — and compares the change it implies over 100 years with the change
actually observed over each population's last 50 years (as pre-specified).

```{python}
#| label: c11-longrun
#| code-summary: "MDMx's long-run age-specific sex difference: the rate per population, and Sweden over 100 years (cached)"
OV = F["overall"]
LR_H = int(OV["longrun_horizon"])
lr_origin = int(years[-1])
lr_jobs = fc.cv_jobs(observed, pops, years, [lr_origin], LR_H, F["min_train_years"], 0)
lr_set = dataclasses.replace(SET, horizon=LR_H)
lr = artifacts.stage(
    "forecast_longrun",
    functools.partial(fc.mdmx_origin, M, observed, pops, years, lr_origin, lr_jobs, lr_set, workers=WORKERS,
                      anchor=E["mdmx_anchor"]),
    inputs=["tensor"], params={"settings": lr_set.as_dict(), "jobs": artifacts.content_hash(lr_jobs),
                               "anchor": E["mdmx_anchor"]},
    code=MDMX_CODE, desc=f"MDMx forecasts {LR_H} years ahead from {lr_origin} (long-run sex differences)")
lr_p = SET.n_pc
lr_target = lr["jobs"][[f"target_{i + 1}" for i in range(lr_p)]].to_numpy()          # (J, p), per year
# The HMD part of each target: w_HMD·δ_HMD, or all of it where the population's own drift was undefined.
lr_hmd = (np.where(lr["jobs"]["own_drift"].to_numpy(bool), SET.weight_hmd, 1.0)[:, None]
          * lr["hmd_drift"][None, :lr_p])
lr_rate = cp.sex_difference_slope(lr["L"], lr_target)                                # (J, A), logit per year
lr_rate_hmd = cp.sex_difference_slope(lr["L"], lr_hmd)


lr_century = 100 * cp.group_means(lr_rate, GROUPS)     # (J, G): change per century implied by the rate
lr_century_hmd = 100 * cp.group_means(lr_rate_hmd, GROUPS)
# Observed: the change of the difference over the last `longrun_lag` years of each population.
lr_obs = cp.observed_sex_difference_change(M, observed, years, [PIDX[p_] for p_ in lr["jobs"]["pop"]], GROUPS,
                                           lag=int(OV["longrun_lag"]), window=int(OV["longrun_window"]))
lr_tab = pd.DataFrame({
    "100 y (median)": np.median(lr_century, axis=0),
    "100 y, HMD part (median)": np.median(lr_century_hmd, axis=0),
    "|100 y| (median)": np.median(np.abs(lr_century), axis=0),
    "last 50 y observed (median)": np.median(lr_obs, axis=0),
    "|last 50 y| (median)": np.median(np.abs(lr_obs), axis=0),
}, index=list(GROUPS))
for lab, row in lr_tab.iterrows():
    word = lab.split()[0]
    latex.report(f"fcLongrunCentury{word}", row["|100 y| (median)"], digits=2,
                 desc=f"MDMx: median |long-run change of the male-female logit difference| per century, {lab}")
    latex.report(f"fcLongrunObserved{word}", row["|last 50 y| (median)"], digits=2,
                 desc=f"Median |observed change of the male-female logit difference| over the last 50 years, {lab}")
latex.report("fcLongrunOrigin", lr_origin, text=str(lr_origin), desc="Origin of the long-run forecasts")
latex.report("fcLongrunPops", len(lr["jobs"]), desc="Populations forecast in the long-run check")
latex.report("fcLongrunObsPops", len(lr_obs), desc="Populations with 55 observed years for the observed change")
# Sweden, 100 years ahead: e₀ of the two sexes and their gap.
lr_sw = lr["points"][lr["points"]["pop"] == SHOW].pivot(index="year", columns="sex", values="e0_fc")
lr_gap = lr_sw["female"] - lr_sw["male"]
latex.report("fcLongrunGapSWEStart", float(lr_gap.iloc[0]), digits=1,
             desc=f"MDMx: female-male e0 gap of {SHOW}, first forecast year from {lr_origin}")
latex.report("fcLongrunGapSWEEnd", float(lr_gap.iloc[-1]), digits=1,
             desc=f"MDMx: female-male e0 gap of {SHOW}, {LR_H} years ahead")
# Like for like: the observed change scaled to a century.
change_ratio = lr_tab["|100 y| (median)"] / (100 / int(OV["longrun_lag"]) * lr_tab["|last 50 y| (median)"])
slower = [lab.lower() for lab in change_ratio.index[change_ratio < 1]]
latex.report("fcLongrunMinYears", F["min_train_years"],
             desc="Observed years up to the origin a population needs for the long-run check")
latex.report("fcLongrunHorizon", LR_H, desc="Horizon (years) of the long-run MDMx forecasts")
latex.report("fcLongrunLag", int(OV["longrun_lag"]), desc="Years over which the observed change of the sex difference is measured")
latex.report("fcLongrunGroups", len(change_ratio), desc="Age groups of the long-run check")
latex.report("fcLongrunSlowerGroups", len(slower),
             desc="Age groups in which the forecast changes the sex difference more slowly than observed (per century)")
lr_note = (f"Over 100 years the model's long-run rate changes the male − female logit difference by a median "
           f"{lr_tab['|100 y| (median)'].min():.2f}–{lr_tab['|100 y| (median)'].max():.2f} across the age groups, "
           f"against {lr_tab['|last 50 y| (median)'].min():.2f}–{lr_tab['|last 50 y| (median)'].max():.2f} actually "
           f"observed over the last {int(OV['longrun_lag'])} years ({len(lr_obs)} populations).  Per century (the "
           "observed change scaled to a century) the forecast sex differences change "
           + ("more slowly than the observed ones in every age group." if len(slower) == len(change_ratio) else
              "at least as fast as the observed ones in every age group." if not slower else
              f"more slowly than the observed ones in {len(slower)} of the {len(change_ratio)} age groups "
              f"({', '.join(slower)}).")
           + f"  For {NAME[SHOW]} the female − male gap in e₀ goes from {lr_gap.iloc[0]:.1f} years in "
             f"{lr_gap.index[0]} to {lr_gap.iloc[-1]:.1f} in {lr_gap.index[-1]}.")
print(lr_note)
lr_tab.round(3)
```

`{python} lr_note`  MDMx therefore forecasts the sexes jointly at every age
without fixing their difference: far ahead it changes at the pace of the
HMD-wide trend of the sex difference, so MDMx is not coherent in the
formal long-run sense (bounded sex ratios), while its sex differences
evolve from one joint model rather than independently.

```{python}
#| label: fig-c11-longrun
#| fig-cap: "MDMx's age-specific sex differences in the long run. Top left: Sweden, male − female logit(q_x) by age — observed in its last observed year and forecast 15, 50 and 100 years ahead. Top right: the long-run rate of change of the male − female difference per century by age, median over the populations (line; band: interquartile range) and the part due to the HMD-wide drift (dashed). Bottom: Sweden, female and male e₀ (left) and their gap (right), observed and forecast 100 years ahead."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8.4))
ax = axes[0, 0]
c_sw = PIDX[SHOW]
t_last = np.flatnonzero(observed[c_sw])[-1]
ax.plot(ages, M[1, :, c_sw, t_last] - M[0, :, c_sw, t_last], color=plotting.COLORS["observed"],
        label=f"observed {years[t_last]}")
sw_idx = lr["schedule_index"].reset_index(drop=True)
shades = plt.get_cmap("Greens")(np.linspace(0.45, 0.95, 3))
for h, colour in zip((15, 50, LR_H), shades):
    row = sw_idx.index[(sw_idx["pop"] == SHOW) & (sw_idx["year"] == lr_origin + h)][0]
    z = lr["schedules"][row]
    ax.plot(ages, z[1] - z[0], color=colour, label=f"forecast +{h} y")
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel("Age"); ax.set_ylabel("Male − female logit($q_x$)"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.set_title(NAME[SHOW], fontsize=10)
ax = axes[0, 1]
q25, q50, q75 = np.percentile(100 * lr_rate, [25, 50, 75], axis=0)
ax.fill_between(ages, q25, q75, color=COLOR["MDMx"], alpha=0.25, lw=0)
ax.plot(ages, q50, color=COLOR["MDMx"], label="median over populations")
ax.plot(ages, np.median(100 * lr_rate_hmd, axis=0), "--", color=COLOR["MDMx"], label="HMD-wide part")
ax.axhline(0, color="grey", lw=0.6)
ax.set_xlabel("Age"); ax.set_ylabel("Change per century (logit)"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.set_title("Long-run rate of the male − female difference", fontsize=10)
obs_sw = truth[(truth["pop"] == SHOW) & (truth["year"] > lr_origin - 60)].pivot(index="year", columns="sex",
                                                                                  values="e0_obs")
ax = axes[1, 0]
for sex, style in (("female", "-"), ("male", "--")):
    ax.plot(obs_sw.index, obs_sw[sex], style, color=plotting.COLORS["observed"])
    ax.plot(lr_sw.index, lr_sw[sex], style, color=COLOR["MDMx"], label=f"{sex}")
ax.set_xlabel("Year"); ax.set_ylabel("$e_0$ (years)"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax = axes[1, 1]
ax.plot(obs_sw.index, obs_sw["female"] - obs_sw["male"], color=plotting.COLORS["observed"], label="observed")
ax.plot(lr_gap.index, lr_gap, color=COLOR["MDMx"], label="MDMx forecast")
ax.set_xlabel("Year"); ax.set_ylabel("Female − male $e_0$ (years)"); ax.legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## How often one start would have been enough {#sec-c11-starts}

The long-run forecasts come from one fit per population at
`{python} lr_origin`, each to the population's whole history, with the
starts of Step 3.  The cell counts the fits in which some start, and those
in which the single moment-based start ($\rho$ in the middle of its
range), ended more than `{python} f"{float(F['mle_start_gap_report']):g}"`
below the maximum log-likelihood.

```{python}
#| label: c11-start-gaps
#| code-summary: "How far below the maximum the starts of the long-run fits ended"
START_GAP = float(F["mle_start_gap_report"])
lr_fits = lr["jobs"]
n_fits = len(lr_fits)
n_gap_any = int((lr_fits["start_gap_max"] > START_GAP).sum())
n_gap_moment = int((lr_fits["moment_gap"] > START_GAP).sum())
# Starts per fit: the best grid points of the profile likelihood, the moment-based start with ρ mid-range,
# and the moment-based starts at each fixed ρ; every fit must have used them all.
n_starts = SET.mle_grid_top + 1 + len(SET.mle_rho_starts)
if not (lr_fits["n_starts"] == n_starts).all():
    raise ValueError(f"The long-run fits used {sorted(lr_fits['n_starts'].unique())} starts, not {n_starts}.")
latex.report("fcNStarts", n_starts, desc="Starts of the optimiser per MDMx fit")
latex.report("fcStartGapThreshold", START_GAP, text=f"{START_GAP:g}",
             desc="Log-likelihood below the maximum at which a start counts as having missed it")
print(f"{n_fits} fits from {lr_origin}: {int(lr_fits['converged'].sum())} converged; best start by kind: "
      f"{lr_fits['best_start_kind'].value_counts().to_dict()}")
print(f"Some start more than {START_GAP:g} below the maximum: {n_gap_any}; the moment-based start: {n_gap_moment}")
latex.report("fcStartGapFits", n_fits,
             desc=f"MDMx fits of the long-run forecasts (one per population, whole history, origin {lr_origin})")
latex.report("fcStartGapAny", n_gap_any,
             desc=f"Long-run fits in which some start ended more than {START_GAP:g} below the maximum log-likelihood")
latex.report("fcStartGapMoment", n_gap_moment,
             desc=f"Long-run fits in which the moment-based start (rho mid-range) ended more than {START_GAP:g} "
                  "below the maximum log-likelihood")
start_note = (f"In {n_gap_any} of the {n_fits} fits at least one start ended more than {START_GAP:g} below the "
              "maximum log-likelihood"
              + (f", and in {n_gap_moment} the moment-based start did: with that start alone, "
                 f"{'that fit' if n_gap_moment == 1 else 'those fits'} would have stopped short of the maximum."
                 if n_gap_moment else
                 f"; the moment-based start came within {START_GAP:g} of the maximum in every fit."))
print(start_note)
```

`{python} start_note`

The structural comparison of the methods, in the companion only, is generated from the settings

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fc-comparison

oa = CMP["open_age"]
R_SESSION = ctx["r_params"]["r"]
R_BL = rbridge.session_info("bayeslife_forecast.R", bl.R_PACKAGES)
dem = f"\\texttt{{demography}} {R_SESSION['packages']['demography']}"
common_data = f"HMD deaths and exposures, ages 0--{oa - 1} and {oa}+"
comparison = pd.DataFrame.from_dict({
    "Data": [common_data, common_data, common_data,
             "$\\operatorname{logit}({}_1q_x)$ of the curated HMD life tables, ages 0--109"],
    "Years used": [f"observed years $\\le$ origin: whole history, or last {WIN} years; "
                   "gaps filled by interpolation"] * 3
                  + [f"own series: observed years $\\le$ origin, whole history or last {WIN} years, "
                     "gaps skipped by the filter; bases, PCA and HMD drift: all populations, "
                     "$\\le$ origin"],

                  "age basis smoothed (\\cref{sec:tucker:bsmooth}); the anchor's residual over age "
                  f"(Whittaker, $\\nu$ = {SET.anchor_smoothing:,.0f})"],
    "Age pattern": ["one fixed $b^{\\mathrm{LC}}_x$ (rank-1 SVD of $\\log m_x$)",
                    f"{CMP['fdm_order']} functional components of $\\log m_x$",
                    f"{CMP['coherent_order_product']} components (product) and "
                    f"{CMP['coherent_order_ratio']} (each ratio)",
                    f"{r2} shared age basis functions; {SET.n_pc} PCA scores of the "
                    f"${r1}\\times{r2}$ core"],
    "Sexes": ["fitted independently", "fitted independently",
              "product--ratio: sex ratios stationary",
              "one model; shared sex and age bases"],
    "Time series": [f"random walk with drift on $k^{{\\mathrm{{LC}}}}_t$ ($k^{{\\mathrm{{LC}}}}_t$ fitted to deaths: \\texttt{{{CMP['lc_adjust']}}})",
                    f"{CMP['fdm_ts_method'].upper()} (automatic) per coefficient",
                    "ARIMA (product), ARFIMA (ratios)",
                    f"damped local linear trend, Kalman filter, $\\rho\\in[{SET.rho_bounds[0]}, "
                    f"{SET.rho_bounds[1]}]$, maximum likelihood"],
    "Other populations": ["none", "none", "none (the two sexes)",
                          f"drift target {SET.weight_hmd}$\\times$HMD-wide + "
                          f"{SET.weight_country}$\\times$own ($W={SET.drift_window}$ years)"],
    "Jump-off": [f"fitted (\\texttt{{{CMP['lc_jumpchoice']}}})",
                 f"fitted (\\texttt{{{CMP['fdm_jumpchoice']}}})", "fitted",
                 "filtered state, plus the observed schedule's residual smoothed over age (persistent anchor)"],
    "Software": [f"\\texttt{{lca}}, {dem}", f"\\texttt{{fdm}}, {dem}",
                 f"\\texttt{{coherentfdm}}, {dem}", "\\texttt{mdmx.forecast}"],
}, orient="index", columns=[LABEL_TEX[m] for m in ("LC", "HU", "CFDM", "MDMx")])
# R prints a package's version with dots (5.3.1); CRAN and the article write the last separator as a hyphen.
bl_ver = R_BL["packages"]["bayesLife"]
bl_ver = bl_ver[::-1].replace(".", "-", 1)[::-1] if bl_ver.count(".") == 2 else bl_ver
comparison.insert(3, LABEL_TEX["BL"], [
    "$e_0$ of the same HMD deaths and exposures",
    f"as Lee--Carter: observed years $\\le$ origin, whole history or last {WIN} years; gaps filled",
    "none",
    "none: forecasts $e_0$ only",
    "female $e_0$ modelled; male $e_0$ from the female--male gap model",
    "double-logistic gain in $e_0$ plus noise, Bayesian hierarchical model (MCMC), annual steps",
    "hierarchical: world parameters from the non-overlapping HMD populations",
    "last observed $e_0$",
    f"\\texttt{{bayesLife}} {bl_ver}"])
comparison.insert(5, LABEL_TEX["FF"], [
    "$\\operatorname{logit}({}_1q_x)$ of the curated HMD life tables, ages 0--109",
    "all populations' observed years $\\le$ origin: the speed on every year, the shape law on the last "
    f"{FFS.shape_window}",
    "each population's $s_1$ over time; the speed and the shape law (LOWESS on $s_1$); the anchor's residual "
    "over age, as anchored MDMx",
    f"MDMx's space: {SET.n_pc} PCA scores; scores 2--{SET.n_pc} follow $s_1$ along the shape law",
    "one model; MDMx's shared sex and age bases",
    "none: $s_1$ moves at the pooled speed of its level; deviations from the shape law decay",
    f"pooled over all populations; beyond the frontier, the {FFS.frontier_k} leading populations' pace",
    "the observed schedule, its residual smoothed over age (persistent anchor)",
    "\\texttt{mdmx.flowfield}"])
comparison = comparison.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "Feature"})
comparison = comparison.rename(columns={LABEL_TEX["MDMx"]: "Anchored MDMx"})
# The table standard: two tables, the established methods and this article's two forecasters, so that each
# fits the page with its text wrapped.
ESTABLISHED = [LABEL_TEX[m] for m in ("LC", "HU", "CFDM", "BL")]
latex.save_table(
    comparison[["Feature", *ESTABLISHED]], "tbl-fc-comparison",
    "The established forecasting methods as they are run in this article.  The two forecasters of this "
    "article are compared in the next table.",
    short_caption="The established forecasting methods",
    wrap={m: "2.9cm" for m in ESTABLISHED}, escape_cells=False)
latex.save_table(
    comparison[["Feature", "Anchored MDMx", LABEL_TEX["FF"]]], "tbl-fc-comparison-forecasters",
    "The two forecasters of this article, under the same headings as the established methods in the previous "
    "table.", short_caption="The two forecasters",
    wrap={"Anchored MDMx": "6.2cm", LABEL_TEX["FF"]: "6.2cm"}, escape_cells=False)
comparison
```

## Summary

MDMx and the flow field forecast the same object, the complete schedule of
both sexes, in the same space, and both start from the observed schedule,
its departure from the scores smoothed over age.
MDMx extrapolates each population's own damped trend, pulled towards the
HMD-wide drift; the flow field moves each population along the paths that
populations at its level of mortality followed, at the leaders' pace beyond
the frontier.  Chapter 12 evaluates both, with the established methods,
from every origin between 1900 and 2015.
